readMe:
THIS FILE IS STEP 1 OF tools/loop/ITERATION-PROMPT.md AND IT MUST STAY READABLE IN ONE Read.
STEP 1 READS THREE FILES, NOT ONE: this file, GATES.md, and PLAN.md §14. A Read has TWO ceilings — it
TRUNCATES past 25,000 tokens and FAILS OUTRIGHT past 256 KB — and BOTH HAVE ALREADY BITTEN THIS FILE.
iter127 hit the byte ceiling: the Read was refused at 459 KB, 397 KB of it the `done` log. iter128
found the TOKEN cap had been truncating for longer and unnoticed, returning lines 1-43 of 92 and
dropping `decisions`, `doneCount`, `doneArchive`, `doneRecent` and `spikes`.

TRUNCATION IS NOT SILENT (corrected iter129): the tool prints an explicit "[Truncated: PARTIAL view]"
notice, so the risk is an agent SKIMMING PAST it, not the tool hiding anything. How the B/tok
constants were derived moved to method-notes.md at iter160; check_calibration owns them now.

RUN `python3 tools/loop/check-state-size.py` AFTER EVERY EDIT TO THIS FILE, TO GATES.md, OR TO
PLAN.md. It measures ALL THREE step-1 files, prints each one's HEADROOM IN KB before it truncates,
distinguishes the two ceilings, lists this file's largest fields, flags every other tools/loop file,
and EXITS NON-ZERO when something stops fitting. WHEN IT TRIPS ON THIS FILE: move an append-heavy
field into an archive under tools/loop/ and leave a short pointer behind. There are EIGHT precedents
— `doneArchive`, `blockersArchive`, `gatesArchive`, `methodNotes`, `scratchInventory`,
`spikesArchive`, `decisions._archive` (iter130, the one keeping its pointer INSIDE the field it
drained) and `doneRecent` (iter151, drained to empty; see `doneRecentNote`, and do not refill it) —
and each asserted its round-trip before this file was rewritten. DO NOT DISCARD CONTENT TO MAKE THE
CHECK PASS: condensing prose you keep is fair payback, dropping archived text is not. WHEN IT TRIPS
ON GATES.md OR PLAN.md: that content is the spec and the gate instructions, so archive a settled
section, never drop one.

AND NOTE WHY THIS PARAGRAPH IS AT THE TOP OF THE FILE RATHER THAN NEXT TO `doneArchive`: a truncated
Read still shows it. iter127's rotation rule was correct and had no effect, because it was written
into a field that sat past the cut. A rule that keeps a file readable is worthless in the half that
gets cut off.
phase:
M6 feature-complete. **ITER170: THE JOB `nextAction` SENT THIS ITERATION AT DID NOT EXIST, AND FINDING THAT OUT UNCOVERED A CONSTANT WRONG IN THE READ PATH FOR 32 ITERATIONS.** Full account: done-archive.jsonl line 171.

  iter169 called "condensing the stub layer" the largest ungated work left, on 22 stubs / 28,434 B. The checker counts **29** — three stub spellings are DECLARED in check-state-size.py and iter169 matched one case-sensitively — and method-notes.md's header had **measured that job and withdrawn it at iter166**. The document with a script behind it was right.

  **THE FIND CAME OUT OF CHASING THAT.** The preamble stated `markdown 2.604 B/tok, JSON 2.368` undated as fact; the live constants are **2.4 / 2.3**. 2.604 is iter129's blend AVERAGE — the methodology check-state-size.py's own docstring names as superseded when iter138 lowered markdown from 2.5. **iter170 read it, used it, and computed 4,674 B of headroom where the checker computes 594 — 8x, on the number deciding whether the file can take another note.** `check_calibration` guards the DEFINITION; a prose copy is a sentence.

  Shipped: **`check_prose_constants`** (check #12) — a ratio in prose must be a live constant or name the iteration that measured it; 3 facts + a vacuity refusal that APPENDS. Fact (3) fired on arrival: **nothing in the orientation layer quoted 2.4 at all.** Guarded by **`mutate-prose-constants.py` at 6/6**, declared in HARNESSES and the runner both ways, and **exempted from its own sweep via HARNESSES** because a harness must carry the defect it plants. **Its grading is proven by a REAL failure, not a synthetic self-check:** 5/6 first run, because a cell reworded two hand-listed ratios while a third sat in the new check's own comment. Also: **the preamble was unguarded by construction** (not a `## ` section, so neither the rotation engine nor `check_method_notes_stubs` could reach its 7,101 B); 15 bullets now sit in two `## ` stubs, covered with **no checker change**. Verified: build 0/0; suite **1394/1394 skipped=0**; run-harnesses **10/10**; checker exit 0 on twelve checks. **Nothing decided, no gate moved.**
nextAction:
**RUN `dotnet build` AND `python3 tools/loop/run-suite.py` BEFORE YOU CHANGE ANYTHING AND AGAIN AFTER YOUR LAST WRITE — NOT `dotnet test | tail`**, which drops the failure lines above the summary (iter154). **Expect 1394 tests**; run-suite.py enforces that itself, plus red on an unparseable summary or any skip — so if it reds on a count, READ THE REASON: a DROP is the signal, and a deliberate one means editing that constant in the same commit and saying why. Several tests sweep the tree's own PROSE outside `tests/`/`tools/`, so a docs-only edit — GATES.md included — can turn it red. **`dotnet test --nologo` RUNS ZERO TESTS AND EXITS 1**; one class is `--filter-query '/*/*/<Class>/*'`, ONE pattern only (iter143).

**DO THE BOOKKEEPING BEFORE run-harnesses.py — ITER170 BURNED A ~7-MINUTE SWEEP ON THIS.** It reported 4/10 with nothing wrong: `iteration` was 170 while `doneCount` and done-archive.jsonl read 169, so `check_done_archive` reddened and every harness using the checker as its BASELINE aborted. **A half-finished state.json fails six guards at once and no message says so.** Order: append the archive line, bump `doneCount`, rewrite `phase`/`nextAction`, THEN sweep.

**FIRST, RUN `git diff tools/loop/state.json` AND `git status`. AN ANSWER FROM MIRKO ARRIVES AS AN UNCOMMITTED EDIT TO THIS FILE** (iter155 found `decisions.formatOnEditHook` that way). **AND `git log --oneline -5` AGAINST `iteration`** — iter169 found two interactive-session commits this file did not mention. **Trust `decisions`/`gates` plus GATES.md's checkboxes over prose in `phase`/`nextAction`** — and **iter170 is the proof this prose can be flatly WRONG, not just stale:** iter169's "22 stub sections / 28,434 B" was hand-derived, disagreed with the checker's 29 (it matched one of THREE declared stub spellings case-sensitively) and contradicted method-notes.md's header since iter166. **RUN THE TOOL BEFORE SPENDING AN ITERATION ON A NUMBER WRITTEN HERE.**

**A GREEN LOCAL BUILD IS NOT A GREEN CI (iter169).** `gh run list --limit 3` is part of verification whenever anything reaches origin: CI resolves a newer SDK and `AnalysisLevel: latest-recommended` follows it, so 0 warnings here can be N errors there. `decisions.analyzerBandDrift`, fully measured. **DO NOT "FIX" IT** — ToolchainPinningTests asserts the hazard is still present. **origin/main is 1 BEHIND** (71799d8 unpushed); no standing push authority — `decisions.pushPolicy`.

**`python3 tools/loop/run-harnesses.py` (10/10, ~7 min) RE-CHECKS EVERYTHING ITERS 162-170 TOUCHED. THE CHECKER SEAM IS SPENT MANY TIMES OVER — DO NOT RE-PROBE:** claim-dimensions (157-8); sibling instances (159-61); container-vs-body enumeration (161); the soft-flag sweep (162-3); PROSE vacuity judgements (164); the DECLARED refusals and return-vs-append (165); stub/body pairing (166); citation resolution (167); harness tracked-ness (168); toolchain pinning (169); prose copies of a constant (170).

**BUDGET — READ BEFORE WRITING A METHOD NOTE; THE OLD ADVICE HERE WAS WRONG.** method-notes.md has **188 B of headroom** (47,812 B of a 48,000 B ceiling), LESS than iter170 started with. **ALL THREE NAMED LEVERS ARE MEASURED AND SPENT:** rotation had ONE candidate worth +28 B; iter170's two preamble rotations netted **-285 B** and **-37 B**, because a stub costs what its headlines cost and those bullets were already terse; iter166 measured condensing boilerplate at ~1.1 KB. **THE ONE LEVER THAT MEASURED WELL IS NEW: REWRITE AN EXISTING VERBOSE STUB AS AN INDEX.** iter169's section rotated with an index stub freed **496 B** from a 1,192 B body, and trimming iter170's own two stubs freed ~800 B more. 30 stubs average ~1,200 B and most restate their bodies instead of pointing at them; the full text is already archived, so **this discards nothing and is the next kilobyte.** Otherwise: WRITE LESS. Destination `tools/loop/method-notes-archive-3.md`, the CURRENT generation; 1 and 2 FULL AND FROZEN. **A generation 4 must be declared in BOTH `ARCHIVE_FILES` and `METHOD_NOTES_GENERATIONS` in the same change — a FAILING CHECK, not advice.** Same rule for THIS file — iter170 tripped state.json's budget too and condensed this field.

**EVERY REMAINING PLAN.md §15 ITEM IS GATED ON MIRKO, AND HAS BEEN FOR ~50 ITERATIONS.** M6 is feature-complete; ten boxes and EIGHT decisions are his. Absent a specific half-edit that ships green today, the index-stub job above is real, bounded, measured work.

**check-state-size.py RUNS TWELVE CHECKS** and nine refuse a vacuous pass. **FIVE DECLARED LISTS MUST BE EDITED IN THE SAME CHANGE AS THE THING THEY DECLARE:** `GATES_ARCHIVE_NON_GATE_KEYS`, `ARCHIVE_FILES`, `METHOD_NOTES_GENERATIONS`, `CITATION_KNOWN_ABSENT`, and **`HARNESSES`, paired BOTH ways with the runner's STEPS** — note iter170's use of it: a harness is EXEMPTED from the prose-constant sweep by being in `HARNESSES`, because a harness must carry the defect it plants. **SETTLING A BLOCKER IS A FOUR-PLACE EDIT** (iter160); the fourth — append the body to blockers-archive.jsonl — is the only one whose omission DESTROYS text (iter155 skipped it). **ROTATING A METHOD NOTE IS A THREE-PLACE EDIT** (iter166). **A REFUSAL APPENDS, IT NEVER `return`s** (iter165). **DO NOT WRITE SPECIMEN PATHS IN PROSE** (iter167); a marketplace action or scoped npm package named in prose parses as a repo path and must resolve on disk (iter169).

**A CONSTANT WRITTEN IN PROSE IS A MIRROR.** `check_prose_constants` fails on a bytes-per-token ratio that is neither a live constant nor attributed to the iteration that measured it. **The live pair is 2.4 B/tok markdown, 2.3 JSON — never copy either undated.**

**THEN CHECK GATES.md. TEN BOXES ARE UNCHECKED, ALL MIRKO'S** — five milestone gates, five side items, mirrored in `gates`; **the checker FAILS ON MIRROR OR STATUS DRIFT**, so trust it. Cheapest first: restart-loop-driver (three commands), gate-m3 (one `approved` label), gate-m4 (one wrong comment), gate-m5 (answer decisions.m5Acceptance), gate-m2 (walk the 44 pages), gate-m6 (push a tag). **EIGHT DECISIONS ARE OPEN, ALL FULLY MEASURED — DO NOT REDO THAT WORK.** What is left in each is a JUDGEMENT the loop must not make. Probes: `.mtk/paths-156/`, `-157/`, `-158/`.

**paste-format-on-edit-hook IS A PURE PASTE, ITS QUESTION SETTLED — DO NOT RE-ASK, AND DO NOT RECREATE `tools/hooks/format-on-edit.py`** (check #10 FAILS if it reappears). **The loop cannot write `.claude/`**; do not retry, do not route around it with an allowlisted `python3`. **tools/loop/docume-loop.sh IS THE ONE FILE AN ITERATION CAN EDIT BUT CANNOT MAKE TAKE EFFECT** — bash parses a `while` loop once and the driver started 2026-07-24, so a "fix" is probably already committed and merely not running (`gates.restart-loop-driver`; iter140 tested it 9/9, NO CODE CHANGE PENDING). Live, re-read by path every pass: ITERATION-PROMPT.md, loop-settings.json.

**MUTATION-HARNESS RULES LIVE IN tools/loop/method-notes.md** (`methodNotes.appendHere`) — read it whole before writing a harness. iter170 added: **a PARTIAL mutation grades the CHECK broken, not the cell** — sweep with a regex and assert none survives.

**HYGIENE, DO NOT DELETE WITHOUT ASKING** (a data file): untracked `tests/golden/.claude/analytics.json` — harmless, but `tests/golden/` is a rule §4.3 contract directory, so a stray `.claude/` there traps a future golden enumerator. Ask Mirko: delete or gitignore? **THE ITER168 FLAKE DID NOT RECUR** in iter169's or iter170's runs (`ConfluenceClientTests.Lists_a_pages_children_...`); **twice in a row IS a find** — look at the children endpoint's stub setup.

blockers._archive: FULL BLOCKER BODIES ARE IN tools/loop/blockers-open.json (moved at iter139; nothing discarded, round-trip asserted — the eighth archive precedent, and like decisions._archive the pointer stays INSIDE the field it drained). Each line below is ONE OPEN blocker: what it is, whose call it is, and where to answer. EVERY ONE IS PHRASED AS A QUESTION FOR MIRKO and every one is also written up at length in GATES.md, which step 1 reads anyway — so open the archive only to ACT on one. NOTE: tools/loop/blockers-archive.jsonl is a DIFFERENT file holding SETTLED blockers. **`blockers` IS AN OBJECT, NOT AN ARRAY** (matching `gates` and `decisions`; nothing reads it programmatically — checked). TO ADD ONE, per protocol step 9: a short kebab-case key here with a ONE-LINE stub ending in a pointer, and the full body in blockers-open.json under the same key. TO SETTLE ONE, **FOUR PLACES, AND check-state-size.py NOW FAILS ON A HALF-EDIT**: delete the key from both, append a one-line verdict to blockersArchive.settled, AND append the body to blockers-archive.jsonl (line shape: `blockersArchive.format`). **THE FOURTH DESTROYS CONTENT IF SKIPPED** - iter155 skipped it. (Condensed iter150 as budget payback; the historical justification for the iter139 move is in blockers-open.json and the done archive.)
blockers.pushPolicy: OPEN, ITER121 — **may the loop push to origin/main?** The same question as `decisions.pushPolicy` in this file, which carries the numbers and the iter130 note; answer it THERE ("always", "on-request" or "never"). Blocks the remote half of gate-m5 and makes gate-m6's tag step misleading; blocks no offline work. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.rule-8-2a: OPEN, ITER75 — **may the §8.2a rule amendment be pasted?** One paste of tools/loop/rule-8-2a-paste.md into .claude/rules/git-workflow.md beneath §8.2. It scopes the force-push exception you already authorised (decisions.compositeAction: floating-v1) so a future iteration cannot read §8.2 literally and delete that work. The loop will not do it itself: it WIDENS force-push authority. Nothing waits on it. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json; full text GATES.md -> paste-rule-8-2a.
blockers.force-push-hook: OPEN, ITER130 — **may the force-push guard be installed?** One paste of tools/loop/loop-settings-paste.md over tools/loop/loop-settings.json. §8.2 is labelled [ENFORCED] but its deny list only covers the flag-first spelling: `git push <remote> HEAD --force` and `--force-with-lease` were both measured ALLOWED. Fix is the committed PreToolUse hook tools/loop/hooks/deny-history-rewrite.py, 25/25, and PROVEN TO LOAD AND FIRE FROM A --settings FILE at iter131, 3/3, without installing anything. **CONFIRMED ITER139: needs NO driver restart** — the running driver re-reads loop-settings.json by path every pass. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.settings-corrections: OPEN, ITER131, TWO ONE-LINERS, NEITHER BLOCKING ANYTHING — (a) this workspace is untrusted (~/.claude.json hasTrustDialogAccepted:false), so three `.claude/settings.json` allow entries are ignored every iteration; zero cost today because --settings supplies a broader rule. (b) `Write(.env)` / `Write(.env.*)` in your GLOBAL settings enforce NOTHING — only `Edit(path)` rules are matched for file permissions. Both found by reading the CLI's own stderr, captured unread into every iteration log for 130 iterations. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.
blockers.restart-loop-driver: OPEN, ITER139 — **will you restart the loop driver?** `touch tools/loop/STOP` -> wait for the pass to end -> `rm tools/loop/STOP` -> `./tools/loop/docume-loop.sh`. The running process started 2026-07-24 14:38:30 and bash parses a `while` loop once, so it is 56.6 h older than docume-loop.sh's newest commit and BOTH commits since (c6fbf1e; 7de6a86, iter137's entire deliverable) have never executed. tools/loop/MODEL is inert for the same reason. NOT blocking the pastes. ITER140: what the restart activates is now TESTED 9/9 and correct (.mtk/paths-140/probe-restart-readiness.py), and the only behaviour change it makes is the model ID string, measured harmless. Probe: .mtk/paths-139/probe-driver-version-drift.py, 8/8. Body: tools/loop/blockers-open.json.

gates.authoritative: GATES.md. It is richer than anything here and step 1 of the protocol tells you to read it; this block is the status mirror rule §9.7 asks for, not a second copy. The full pre-iter128 mirror text is in tools/loop/gates-archive.json.
gates.gate-m1-aurservices-files: CLOSED WITHOUT ACTION 2026-07-25 by Mirko ('just use your golden set'); M1 closed at iter48 (bcf36ba). DO NOT REOPEN — real-corpus validation moved to M7. Struck through in GATES.md with the full reasoning; verbatim mirror in tools/loop/gates-archive.json.
gates.gate-m2-aur-review: PENDING, MIRKO'S. The loop's half finished at iter113: 44 pages are up in DOCUMESBX. Needs your page-by-page review, then the tick. Caveat GATES.md states: cases/mermaid.md is deliberately absent (beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 rejects `graph TD;` and `pie`, and a page fails as a unit) - tick on the rendering you CAN see; the mermaid question is decisions.mermaidDialectGap, not this gate.
gates.gate-m3-approval-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the cheapest of the five: add ONE `approved` label to any published page ('CLI Reference', id 451969089, is a good one), then tick. The loop then runs `sync --labels`, republishes that page with `publish --notify-reviewers`, and you re-approve. `approvedBy` will read 'unknown' and that is correct, not a bug (spike S3: Confluence exposes no label author). THIS GATE ALSO GATES SHIPPED CODE - iter122's `--notify-reviewers` fires only where a run revokes an approval, and no DOCUMESBX page carries one, so nothing can exercise it live until this box moves.
gates.gate-m4-feedback-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S. Write ONE comment saying something factually wrong about a published page (an INLINE comment on a sentence exercises the most code), then tick. The loop then runs `sync --comments` -> `/docs-feedback` -> a `docs/feedback-<date>` PR -> republish -> `sync --reply`.
gates.gate-m5-refresh-roundtrip: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and it is a DECISION not a task: does M5's §14 acceptance run on this repo (copy docs-drift-pr.yml in, add secrets) or fold into M7 where a real repo with real PRs exists? Answer in decisions.m5Acceptance. The live middle of the chain is already done and re-runnable (iter121: `drift --mark` labelled 9 of 11 sourced pages against DOCUMESBX and proved a label spends no page version).
gates.gate-m6-first-release: PENDING, MIRKO'S, and the only irreversible one - a package on a GitHub Packages feed cannot be unpublished, which is why the loop will not do it. Steps: (1) confirm Directory.Build.props <Version>, plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version and plugin/README.md's git-subdir ref all read the number you want (all three read 0.1.0; release.yml's first step refuses a mismatch before building, so a wrong guess costs nothing); (2) `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`; (3) delete the 'Not published yet' note from README.md; (4) tick. The loop then walks the README literally in a fresh empty directory - that walk IS M6's acceptance. A PAT with read:packages in the loop environment is needed for the install half.
gates.paste-rule-8-2a: PENDING, MIRKO'S, ONE PASTE, NOTHING WAITS ON IT — and it was missing from this block from iter75 to iter144, which is why check-state-size.py now derives this mirror from GATES.md. Add the §8.2a bullet to .claude/rules/git-workflow.md directly beneath §8.2, leaving §8.2 itself untouched; the exact text is verbatim in tools/loop/rule-8-2a-paste.md below the `---`. It SCOPES the force-push exception you already authorised (decisions.compositeAction: floating-v1, built at db240dc) so a future iteration cannot read §8.2 literally and delete work you asked for. The loop will not write it even though an allowlisted python3 could: it WIDENS force-push authority, which is what the guard in the way exists to prevent. Full reasoning: GATES.md. Long mirror: tools/loop/gates-archive.json (trimmed iter145).

No restart was needed (this file is re-read by path every pass), so rule §8.2's [ENFORCED] label is now true for flag-anywhere spellings as well as flag-first. Remaining in-situ check for whoever runs next: `git push deny-probe-nonexistent-remote HEAD --force` should be refused with the §8.2 message. Full note in GATES.md.

decisions._archive: FULL DECISION BODIES ARE IN tools/loop/decisions-archive.json, moved there at iter130 because this field was 11.6 KB of the 50 KB that put step 1's Read past its budget. NOTHING WAS DISCARDED and the round-trip was asserted before this file was rewritten (the seventh precedent, after doneArchive, blockersArchive, gatesArchive, methodNotes, scratchInventory and spikesArchive). Each key below is a one-line summary: what the decision is, whose call it is, and what to strike off which test when it is settled. `nextAction` carries the same list in the order worth settling, so orientation costs no extra Read; open the archive only to ACT on one. MIRKO: write your answer straight over the stub in this file — the key is what matters, not the text it replaces.
decisions.mermaidDialectGap: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter113 — **the JUDGEMENT is his; the FACTS were fully measured at iter156 and the loop must not pick an option.** beautiful-mermaid 1.1.3 renders six families and nothing else. Options: (a) upgrade-or-replace, (b) strip a trailing `;` in tools/render-mermaid.mjs, (c) report unsupported dialects as a named degradation instead of failing the page. iter156's four findings — 1.1.3 IS `dist-tags.latest`, so (a) means REPLACE or nothing; the gap is 17 diagram types and not 1; the semicolon rejection is an inconsistency INSIDE the library, which is what makes (b) cheap; and YAML frontmatter fails on every type including the six that work — moved to the body at iter162, verbatim, round-trip asserted. Full write-up: GATES.md's mermaid block. Body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json.
decisions.m5Acceptance: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter121. Where M5's §14 acceptance runs: (a) install docs-drift-pr.yml here and open one PR (no secrets needed), (b) add secrets + docs-refresh/docs-publish, which makes every push to main publish to the sandbox, or (c) fold into M7 and reword §14. Also gate-m5. Interacts with pushPolicy. Full body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json. **ITER157 MEASURED BOTH BUILDABLE OPTIONS AND NEITHER COSTS WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE: (a) IS ZERO-SECRET, AND (b) IS NARROWER THAN ITS DESCRIPTION** (docs-publish.yml is filtered to paths:['docs/wiki/**'], docs-refresh.yml is not push-triggered at all) — the numbers moved to the body at iter163, verbatim, round-trip asserted.
decisions.pushPolicy: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter121. May the loop `git push origin main`? Answer "always", "on-request" or "never". **ITER169: THE FACTS UNDER THIS QUESTION CHANGED. An interactive session pushed at f2308b4, so origin/main is CURRENT (0 ahead, 0 behind) — it was 107 behind at 699c855 when this was written — and CI now runs on every push.** That was an action taken with you present, NOT an answer: the loop still has no standing authority and will not push. It also settled the iter130 caveat in the loop's favour — the force-push guard is installed (gate paste-force-push-hook, DONE), so the hole this decision used to widen is closed. Still blocks the remote half of gate-m5. Full body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json and the blockers array.
decisions.planSection6Deviations: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter122. §6's preamble declares three global options that did not ship as declared: `--verbose` built NOWHERE, `--json` built on `status` alone (`drift` spells it `--format`), `--config` absent from `init`/`convert`. Either BUILD them (three slices) or CORRECT §6. Then strike the entry off `UnbuiltOptions` in tests/DocuMe.Core.Tests/Acceptance/PlanCommandSpecTests.cs. Full body: tools/loop/decisions-archive.json. **ITER157: NOTHING SHIPPED DEPENDS ON THE THREE UNBUILT OPTIONS, so correcting §6 breaks no consumer and building them unblocks nothing that is asking** — already a standing assertion via CliReferencePageTests; the file-by-file measurement moved to the body at iter163, verbatim, round-trip asserted.
decisions.planSection5Deviations: OPEN, MIRKO'S, iter123. Two config fields load, validate, round-trip and are read by NO line of src/: `links.repoBlobUrl` and `drift.defaultBranch`. Build or delete each. Then strike off `DeadFields` in PlanDataContractTests.cs AND delete the bullet from docs/wiki/20-reference/configuration.md's inert section — the test fails from both sides. Settle with planSection10Deviations (a). **ITER157: THE PROMISE SURFACE IS SIX SHIPPED FILES PER KNOB, NOT THREE, AND TWO SKILLS NAME repoBlobUrl**, pinned in both directions, so A HALF-STRIKE FAILS THE SUITE FROM BOTH SIDES: strike or build in all six and update Places in the same change.
